precepts.text: Submit yourselves therefore to God: take the counsel. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. How do you resist him? By submitting to God first. Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. How do you draw nigh? You come to the house of learning, somebody teaches you, and God draws nigh back to you and gives you a way to escape. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.
precepts.point: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life. How do you know what you can endure unless you go through it? You do not know if you can lift the weight until it is on the rack. You are asking for muscles; well, you have to lift.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God.” You want to blame somebody: Lord, it ain’t me, you put that big booty woman in front of me. The Lord says stop, bro. I put the nine millimeter in front of you, but you didn’t shoot yourself; I put the knife in your hand; I put the crack pipe in the room, but you didn’t smoke it. “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Enticed is when something appeals to you and you give in; you entertain it. That is on you; that is your choice. God is just showing you what your vice is, and now that is what you are fighting.

When you are tempted, you are supposed to resist. James tells how: “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” Submit yourself to God: take the counsel. How do you resist the devil? By first submitting yourself to God.

“Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you.” How are you going to draw nigh to God? Somebody is going to teach you and you are going to learn; you go to the house of learning. That is what you are doing now. And God will draw nigh to you and give you a way to escape. “Blessed is the man that endureth temptation.” How do you know what you can endure unless you go through it? You don’t know you can bench 315 until it is on the rack. You are asking for muscles; you have to lift.

“Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” We just read that in chapter one: “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” Now that you hear the correction about how to get right with God, you have excuses. You see the sin in front of you and turn away, like seeing a booger in your nose in the mirror and turning your head; the booger is still there. “receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls. But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only.” The glass is the Bible; you see yourself in it and walk away and forget. You can close the book; you are still a sinner. Submit, resist, draw nigh, and cleanse your hands.

precepts.text: For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work. The word of God is pure and there is no variableness in it; there should be no confusion in what is being said. The confusion is that wisdom which descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish: it is deceiving you. Then you wonder why good things are withheld from you and why you cannot move forward.
precepts.point: Every captain who has sat in counsel knows the look: you tell a person what they are doing wrong, and they squint, get confused, and repeat back the very thing you just said. It is the battle in the mind at that moment; right is coming in, and wrong is warring against it.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
James 4:1 asks, “From whence come wars and fightings among you?” When you are told something you are doing wrong and something in you is adverse to correction, right is coming in and wrong is warring against it. Captains who have sat in counsel know the look: you tell somebody they don't listen, and they squint like they are confused and repeat back what you just said. It ain't their sight that went bad. It is the battle in the mind, manifesting in the face.

James shows where that confusion comes from: “For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.” The word of God is pure; there is no variableness in it, and there should be no confusion in what is being said. If you were sincere, you would say, show me the lie, help me understand, maybe I am in error. Instead you are confused, because you are warring with what is right and don't want to accept it. You have strife in your heart.

“This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.” It is deceiving you, the same deceiving we read in chapter one.

Then you wonder why good things are withheld from you and why you can't move forward. You are a liar, a thief, a murderer, an adulterer, it is being identified to you, and you cannot reason with yourself. You are struggling with yourself, and that is the war in your members.

precepts.text: Speak not evil one of another, brethren: when brothers get corrected and do not like it, they start speaking evil of the ones who corrected them. What are you supposed to do instead? Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord.
precepts.point: Every captain who has sat in counsel knows the look: you tell a person what they are doing wrong, and they squint, get confused, and repeat back the very thing you just said. It is the battle in the mind at that moment; right is coming in, and wrong is warring against it.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
When a brother starts to correct you and you don't like it, what do brothers start doing? They get mad, they pull away, they hold a grudge, and then they start speaking evil of the ones who corrected them. James says: “Speak not evil one of another, brethren.”

What are you supposed to do instead? “Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord.” You are supposed to humble yourself in the sight of the Lord, because you know to do good, but you don't want to do it.

That is the war and the fighting of James 4:1, coming out of the lusts that war in your members. The correction comes in, the wrong inside wars against it, and instead of humbling yourself, the war turns outward into speaking evil of your brother. The one who humbles himself stops the war where it starts.

precepts.text: Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin. You know what is being said is right, but you do not want to do it, because that sin is what you are struggling with. People in the streets want to fight the brothers just for teaching the Bible, because it convicts them.
precepts.point: Every captain who has sat in counsel knows the look: you tell a person what they are doing wrong, and they squint, get confused, and repeat back the very thing you just said. It is the battle in the mind at that moment; right is coming in, and wrong is warring against it.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.” You know that what is being said is right, but you don't want to do it, because you are struggling. What is sin for you? Your sin is what you are struggling with. That is where the war is: you don't want to accept the prophet telling you.

That is all the people in the streets right now. You tell them what they are doing wrong and they are ready to kill you; they want to fight you for teaching the Bible. What's wrong with you? You hate to hear it because it convicts you. It is letting you know your life is in shambles, that you are evil, that you are the devil.

So the wars and fightings of James 4:1 come from knowing to do good and not doing it. The lust you are holding on to wars against the good you already know.

precepts.text: Precept brought by the captain on justifying yourself: if I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me. The margin renders justify as cleanse or clear self. Deceiving yourself is telling yourself, I am already cleansed, I am already clear, while refusing the reproof and instruction the teachers bring. Video played in class: sometimes you have to let people suffer the consequences of choices they made knowingly, because rescue delays the learning; growth delayed by rescue is growth denied. As David said, it is good that I was afflicted. Teachers cannot carry everybody; and teachers, do not weaponize the scriptures either: do not be the brother that is wise and teacheth many, and is unprofitable to himself, holding brothers to an accountability you will not hold yourself to.
precepts.point: Every captain who has sat in counsel knows the look: you tell a person what they are doing wrong, and they squint, get confused, and repeat back the very thing you just said. It is the battle in the mind at that moment; right is coming in, and wrong is warring against it.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
Part of deceiving yourself is justifying yourself. “If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me”. You are condemning yourself. The word of God, which comes from the teachers, is supposed to cleanse you, and the margin gives justify as cleanse, or clear self. So justifying yourself is deceiving yourself into thinking, I'm already cleansed, I'm already clear. Whatever the teachers have to say, the reproof and the instruction I'm receiving, I'm already clean.

When that happens, teachers, sometimes you have to let people suffer. Most people don't make the same mistake twice by accident; they choose, ignore the warnings, repeat the patterns, and expect someone else to absorb the consequences. Rescue delays the learning, and growth delayed by rescue is growth denied. David said it was good that he was afflicted. We can't carry everybody.

But teachers and instructors cannot weaponize the scriptures either, using them to correct everybody else and never our own lives. Then you are the brother that is wise and teacheth many, yet is unprofitable to himself, holding brothers to a higher accountability than you are willing to hold yourself, expecting perfection while you have hidden sins. The justified self is the one the mouth condemns, whether it is the one being corrected or the one correcting.

precepts.text: From whence come wars and fightings among you? Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain. Simon wanted the upper hand over Onias and couldn't get it. Ye have not, because ye ask not; and when ye ask and receive not, it is because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts: a lustful purpose that is not for the benefit of the nation.
precepts.point: But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon's faction murders were committed: Simon hated Onias so much he had one of his men kill one of Onias's priests. That is why I say it is never just one thing; it is a domino effect of sins.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
“But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon’s faction murders were committed”. Simon hated Onias the third so much that he had one of his men kill one of Onias’s priests. That is why it is never just one thing; it is a domino effect of sins. James shows where it comes from.

“From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members? Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain”. Simon wanted the upper hand over Onias, and he could not get it. So what did he do?

“ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not.” Because you are not praying to the Lord about it. “Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.” When you pray and still do not receive, it is because you ask for the wrong reasons. You have a lustful purpose behind it, a purpose that is not for the benefit of the nation.

This is a self-examination class for all of us: these are the attributes of Simon.

precepts.text: Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.
precepts.point: Friendship with the world is enmity with God, and makes you an adulterer against him.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
“From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members?” It is a consistent battle between the spiritual man and the carnal man. “Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have”: you slander the brother or sister who has what you want, give them the evil eye, speak nasty. You ask for a home, a car, a wife, and receive not, because you “ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts”: to show off, to stunt, to have a trophy wife, to be seen of men.

Christ said if you love the world, you hate me. John writes it: “Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.” Love not this captivity, neither the precious things and riches in this captivity, neither the mansion on the hill, not even your damn job. A lot of brothers love their jobs more than they love this truth.

These things are hooks inside of you that will pull you out of this truth. They are devices of Satan, the tangible trinkets he gives, which our brothers and sisters lust after as status symbols when the kingdom of heaven is at hand. In Babylon everything is accessible at your fingertips, and everything as far as your eye can see appeals to the flesh.

If any man loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. That is why James says “the friendship of the world is enmity with God.” Enmity means the state of being actively opposed or hostile, a feud, conflict, bitterness, resentment. That is the mentality that says why do I have to keep the Sabbath, I could be at home, the boxing match is on today. Some sneak off for Christmas and come back with fifteen presents in the trunk. You hate God and God’s laws. This captivity, the dominion of your oppressor, is going to go, and if you don’t kill that old man and that old woman, you are going with him. Kill or be killed.

precepts.text: No man can serve two masters; ye cannot serve God and mammon.
precepts.point: Friendship with the world is enmity with God, and makes you an adulterer against him.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
On the line of adultery and lust and the love of the world, Christ said: “No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.”

A decision has to be made. Either you hate God, have enmity against him, and love the other, or you hold to the one and despise the other. The other can be money, your career, your bed because you don’t want to be here, a Christmas stocking full of abominations. Some snuck off and celebrated the devastation of their brothers, the slaughter of the tribe of Gad, got a turkey drumstick, watched the football game, then came back saying shalom, Most High in Christ bless. Many will hold on to the world and despise the heavenly Father.

You cannot serve the God of the nation of Israel and mammon. Brothers and sisters are more loyal to their jobs and the white man who runs the corporations, who can terminate your contract after fifteen years of loyalty just as you are getting ready to retire. That is serving mammon.

James calls it what it is: “Ye adulterers and adulteresses.” When these other things have become a god, you have committed adultery against the heavenly Father. Many do not hate the world; they hate having to change and repent. That is the war in your members, and you have to kill that adulterous spirit inside you or it will kill you.

precepts.text: Sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.
precepts.point: Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double minded.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
God “resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.” The humble submit to God and resist the devil, and James goes on: “Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” How do we purify our minds? Paul shows how Christ cleanses his people: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.”

In Christianity many think that because they dipped themselves in water they are a whole other person. But the true baptism is washing yourself with the word. Sitting here in the class, hearing the scriptures, is that washing. And to sanctify and cleanse by the washing of water by the word means you have to keep the commandments. That is the way you cleanse yourself.

The hands are cleansed of your evil works and evil ways, and the heart is purified of the old worldly mindset. The double minded are the brothers who want to be here but do not want to be here, one foot in and one foot out the door. That is lukewarm, and the Lord will spew the lukewarm out, which means he will put you to death. So either you are hot and kill that old man with the word, or you are lukewarm and you will be killed. Either way, somebody has to die.

The humble who receive that grace are the ones taking steps to kill the old man, sharpening their swords with the word to subdue the evil spirit that plagued them for years before they knew this glorious gospel. That washing is how the Lord draws nigh to them.

precepts.text: The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.
precepts.point: Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double minded.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
James says God “giveth grace unto the humble”, and calls on them: “Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” Paul says Christ cleanses his people “with the washing of water by the word.” David shows what that word is and what it does: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.”

The law of the Lord is perfect, and that is what is going to cleanse you. That is what makes you perfect. Keeping the commandments is the cleansing. It converts the soul: it turns the old man into a new man, and makes the simple wise.

That is how you purify your mind. Remove from you the old ways, the old worldly mindset. You cannot get that cleansing from the white man's couch or from cashing a check; pay all the bills and you will still feel empty without the Lord in your life. Submit yourselves to his will, to his law, statutes and commandments, and resist the devil, the deceiver: his lies, the Trinity, the apologetics, the false doctrines of the other nations, and the world, point blank, period.

The more you apply the law and read, the more the Lord draws nigh to you and opens his understanding to you: the dark mysteries and the parables, how to guide your household, and how to stand in the temptations, trials and lusts that come your way. The perfect law is the weapon that kills the old man.

precepts.text: God resisteth the proud but giveth grace unto the humble; submit yourselves to God, resist the devil, draw nigh to God, cleanse your hands and purify your hearts, the very thing we need in these last days.
precepts.point: The Lord rewarded David according to his righteousness and the cleanness of his hands, for he kept the ways of the Lord and did not wickedly depart from his God; all the Lord's judgments were before him and he did not depart from his statutes. He kept himself from his own iniquity, holding back his flesh; the one time it overtook him he was judged and got right back on track, for a righteous man falls and rises again.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble. Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.”

David sang, “The Lord rewarded me according to my righteousness: according to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me. For I have kept the ways of the Lord, and have not wickedly departed from my God.” All the Lord’s judgments were before him, and he did not depart from his statutes. His hands were clean, and the Lord delivered him.

Submit to God, resist the devil, draw nigh to God, cleanse your hands and purify your hearts: that is the very thing we need in these last days.

precepts.text: Ye ask and receive not because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts; do not pray for enemies to fall so you can stunt on them, but so you can continue to do his will uninterrupted.
precepts.point: Delight thyself in the Most High and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart; commit thy way unto him and he shall bring it to pass.

note.label: Psalm 37: Fret Not Because of Evildoers

precepts.why:
“he shall give thee the desires of thine heart”, yet James shows why so many ask and get nothing: “Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.” The desire of the heart has to be according to his will.

So do not pray for your enemies to fall so you can stunt on them; pray that they fall so you can continue to do his will uninterrupted. Commit your way to the Most High by keeping the commandments and trusting him, and “he shall bring forth thy righteousness as the light, and thy judgment as the noonday.”

precepts.text: A lot of times we desire things but do not receive them because we do not ask; ye have not because ye ask not.
precepts.point: When we read our four chapters we should read to understand, seeing how the examples of our forefathers and foremothers can be used for us.

note.label: Psalm 142: The Lord My Refuge and Portion

precepts.why:
“Attend unto my cry; for I am brought very low: deliver me from my persecutors; for they are stronger than I.” David asks. “Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain: ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not.” A lot of times we desire things but do not receive them because we do not ask.

David has a level of humility to say his persecutors are stronger than him. To have enemies stronger than you, you have to be willing to let the powers we have take that place instead of trying to handle it yourself.

precepts.text: When you do ask and receive not, it is because you ask amiss, to consume it upon your own lust.
precepts.point: When we read our four chapters we should read to understand, seeing how the examples of our forefathers and foremothers can be used for us.

note.label: Psalm 142: The Lord My Refuge and Portion

precepts.why:
“Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.” When you do ask and receive not, it is because you ask amiss, to consume it upon your own lust. David asked for deliverance and for his soul to be brought out of prison so that he might praise the name of the Most High, not for his lusts.

You can ask the Lord for something and then do the opposite; when you pray you should put in the effort to make it happen. If you want a house, a wife, or a husband, you have to put in the work.

precepts.text: You do not know what shall be tomorrow, for life is a vapor; you ought to say, if the Most High wills, we shall do this or that.
precepts.point: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips. Do not be boastful.

note.label: Proverbs 27: Boast Not of Tomorrow

precepts.why:
“Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.” James says the same: “Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.”

You do not know what will be tomorrow, for your life is a vapor. So James says what you ought to say instead: “For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.” If the Most High wills, we will do this or that.

None of us knows how much time we have; the Most High draws the line. Moses spoke unadvisedly at the waters of strife and was told he would not enter the promised land, and though he died in full strength at 120, the Most High set the end of his days. That is why you do not boast of tomorrow, and why you let another man praise you and not your own mouth.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 8 A Star Called Wormwood

precepts.why:
What is a hindrance? This is how we can get our prayers answered, slowly but surely. “Ye ask,” Ye ask, meaning you prayed; when it says ask it is talking about prayer. “and receive not,” God is not answering your prayers. Why? “because ye ask amiss,” You ask for the wrong reasons; you are praying amiss, praying for the wrong reason. “that ye may consume it upon your lusts.” Like some of you cougars, or alley cats: you have women praying here, the sister is 40 or 50 and she wants the 20-year-old brother as a husband, and wants to know why God ain't answering my prayer. That is not his will, sister; that young boy wants children; you are past your prime. Leave the little boy alone, let him grow up and struggle with a girl his age. Here goes the older woman: go get the Icy Hot, put it on my back, my arthritis is kicking in. This young boy wants to do flips and somersaults in the bedroom. A sister came up to the table, said she was 46, her face said every bit of 56, and she wanted the 25-year-old brother that goes to the gym religiously, the one with the narrow waist and the wide shoulders. Did you look in the mirror, sister? She was a circle. I go to the gym; I don't know what you are doing in there. That is not his will, that you mess that boy's life up. In one of the schools a young brother married a wife way older, and it turned out he took out three life insurance policies on her; Tyler Perry has a movie about that, A Fall from Grace, a good movie: an older woman fell in love with a young strapping man and he used and abused the hell out of her. You want somebody to grow old together with; how are you growing old together if he is 20 and you are 40? When he is 40 she is 60. You have run past the finish line. When she hits menopause, that man is going to leave you. That is why we tell you all those marriages don't work, but you don't listen to us; you said to hell with the deacons and the bishop and did your own thing. We are just keeping it real, keeping it a hundred.

You are not following the will of God in your prayers; you are not balancing what you want according to God's word. That is why some of you brothers can't get married. One particular brother chases all these women: Bishop, show the sister my picture, I'm very handsome. We show it to the sister: oh hell no, don't do that to me, Bishop, don't ruin my life with that dude. Several times. Then a young lady pops up who likes him, and he says I don't like her, I don't want her. You are simple. Some people you can't help; let them rot. They chase something outside of their shoe size: if your size is eight, you wear eight. Like sisters back in the world who know they are a size 14 and buy a pair of pants that is a size 8, looking like the Michelin Man squeezed into them pants.

And you brothers with your jobs, praying God bless me with a job. God wants you to get a job, but some of you brothers are very talented, very smart, and your character is messed up. Talent will get you in the door, but your character will keep you in the room. Negroes don't understand that: you have the talent to get to the door, but you have to bring forth your character to make the interviewer like you: be on time, do what you are supposed to do on a daily basis, don't come with attitude, don't be lazy. You make excuses when people try to check you on your character, so we just leave you alone: he is going to fizzle out.

That ye may consume it upon your lusts, your pleasures: you are not praying for the right reasons. Some sisters pray for a particular house only because sister so-and-so has a house like that; she is in competition with this sister. I want a house better than her house, a pair of shoes better than her shoes, a head covering better than her head covering. Trying to keep up with the Joneses; people like that always go broke. That is why we made a uniform for the sisters: one sister came in with two-inch heels, the next week another with four-inch heels, then six, then eight; heel competitions. And a brother said he married a sister out of charity, he felt sorry for her; I think the charity went the other way. Be real with yourself: if you can't be real with me or the deacons, be real with yourself.

note.label: The Art of War - Rules of Engagement

points: Read. It says, resist the devil. Resist what? If your eye be single, what are you resisting?

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

points: But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble. Truly, God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble. But many of us do not know if there is pride in us.

There are two kinds of pride, both good and bad. Good pride represents our dignity and self-respect. Bad pride is the deadly sin of superiority that reeks of conceit and arrogance. So arrogance, superiority, that kind of pride is the pride God does not like. Superiority is thinking I am better, I am greater, I want to be better than you. Or arrogance — nobody can say anything to you, you do not want to listen to anybody.

Usually kids do not deal with that. When a child is very young they do not deal with that. They listen. You tell them get over there, do this, do that, and at a young age they listen. It is as they get older that they start to develop these demons, pride and egos. A child is also quick to forgive, and a child does not deal with fear.

Ten signs of pride in you that you may not know. One, always wanting to win or be first. Was that the spirit on the apostles? That showed they were men — but they corrected it. We should not always want to be first. All about me, me. That is pride in a negative way.

Two, talking a lot about yourself. Me, me, me. I am so good, I am so this. That is pride in a negative way. You are self-absorbed. Every time I look at you, you are on your phone taking selfies. If I offend any of you sisters, I am sorry, but you know who I am talking about. I curse my daughters out, I said you had better not be self-absorbed, I do not want to see you taking selfies all the time. And some of you brothers too — you start working out, you get a little muscle, and you are always taking pictures.

Three, not admitting when you are wrong. That is pride, which is also ego. You do not want to say you are wrong when you are wrong, because your ego will not allow you to. The scripture says take the load — if you have it out with your brother, take the load, I apologise, and we can keep moving. But pride will not let you do it. I am not saying I am sorry; you have got to say you are sorry first.

Four, thinking you are better than others. If you think you are better than your brothers and sisters, that is pride. I am not better than any of you, and I do not roll like that. That spirit should not be rolling even among leaders. Oh, I am a better teacher than you, I can break down the scripture better than you. When you start thinking like that, that is pride. And guess who sees it? The Lord. He reads your mind.
Five, being unwilling to learn from others. You do not want to learn from others because you think you know everything, and you have a shut mind.

Six, acting like rules do not apply to you. The rules also apply to everybody, including myself, including the deacon. We cannot make the rules and then break the rules. And the laws that God set up go into that also.
Seven, ignoring or dismissing other people's ideas. People come up with something good and you say, no, I do not like that. Why do you not work together and get this done? That is pride.
Eight, making fun of others. Nine, refusing to help or collaborate with others. You do not want to help anyone and you are not willing to work together. That is pride.

Ten, being overly focused on your appearance or status. Meaning the restructuring that we did — some of you brothers were taken down and thought it was the end of the world. I am not an officer of fifty any more. Some brothers even gave up their rank. We made them officers of ten, and brothers said, I do not want any rank, I am just going to be a brother in the congregation. That is pride. Whatever status you are at, do the work. Why is it so hard for you? Because you want to be over brothers and rule over brothers. You are not doing it sincerely. When we did the restructure and you see brothers bug out, they are not here sincerely.

And I hear some sisters saying, oh, I am an officer so-and-so, so that means I am over sisters. We never made you over anyone. We have a system set up for the senior sisters, but your job is to set an example and help these sisters, and when they come to you for advice you give them scriptural advice. And the sisters we set up over these things are not necessarily an officer's wife — it is the sisters that are equipped, that are sincere, that we know can handle it. Some of you brothers think because you are an officer of fifty your wife is over all the sisters. She is not, unless she has got those gifts and skills.

note.label: The Mind of a Child: Void of Ego and Pride

points: Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. The scenario I just gave is part of resisting, because he is going to tempt you to keep it quiet, keep it silent, keep it under wraps, nobody is going to know. But if you do that, that is not resisting the devil. That is actually doing what he told you to do.

Every captain who has sat in counsel knows the look: you tell a person what they are doing wrong, and they squint, get confused, and repeat back the very thing you just said. It is the battle in the mind at that moment; right is coming in, and wrong is warring against it.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

points: From whence come wars and fightings among you? Come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members? Something inside is making the conflict come up all the time. Whether it is the government, the congregation, your house, or your marriage, be honest about where the trouble starts. That is why we do counsel and hear both sides: once you let them speak enough, you can say, you are the reason there is no peace.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain. No matter how much you fight, you have nothing. He has everything and it is not enough for him.

points: Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts. There is a way to ask according to the Lord; and some people you are not going to have peace with. If the scripture cannot fix them, there is nothing you can do for them: examine the life of the person, send them on their way, and guard your peace.

Purify your hearts, ye double minded: your body is here on the Sabbath and your mind is somewhere else.
